_README: Label id -> structure name for the Visible Human MALE pelvic floor and perineum volume (scripts/cryo/vhm_pelvic_floor_from_cryo.py), plus the mapping onto atlas entities. A KEY, not data. rule-based: markers by position rules relative to his bone and organ labels (including the prostate), boundaries by marker watershed on the pale septa of his cryosection photographs; compartments are muscles the photographs do not separate (mapped to null).
source: U.S. National Library of Medicine, The Visible Human Project (public domain), MALE colour cryosections (1 mm, resampled onto the legs-block CT grid) and CT via the NCI Imaging Data Commons; TotalSegmentator v2.18.0 `total` labels (legs_total.nii.gz, the legs CT block -- his torso block does not reach the perineum, see the module docstring) as anchors and exclusions. Rules from Standring S (ed.), Gray's Anatomy, 42nd ed., ch. 62 'True pelvis, pelvic floor and perineum', and Moore KL et al., Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed., ch. 6 'Pelvis and Perineum'. Derived data (scripts/cryo/vhm_pelvic_floor_from_cryo.py), rule-based, ported from scripts/cryo/vhf_pelvic_floor_from_cryo.py.

not_shipped.obturator_internus: the obturator internus is not a Q68 target; it is carried as a sink so that the muscle lying on the inner surface of the ischium is not attributed to the levator ani, which arises from the tendinous arch on its fascia
not_shipped.perineal_other: sink for the rest of the perineal muscle mass -- the crus and body of the corpus cavernosum where not claimed by ischiocavernosus, and the urethral wall, which photograph as dark as striated muscle at 1 mm; it keeps that tissue out of the bulbospongiosus and the ischiocavernosus
not_shipped.superficial_transverse_perineal_right: 0.9 cm3 on this side, under the 1.0 cm3 a 1 mm frame supports as a named muscle
not_shipped.superficial_transverse_perineal_left: 0.7 cm3 on this side, under the 1.0 cm3 a 1 mm frame supports as a named muscle
not_shipped.pubococcygeus: carried inside levator_ani: no septum between the levator's parts at 1 mm
not_shipped.puborectalis: carried inside levator_ani: no septum between the levator's parts at 1 mm
not_shipped.iliococcygeus: carried inside levator_ani: no septum between the levator's parts at 1 mm
not_shipped.external_urethral_sphincter: a 3-5 mm collar on the membranous urethra in the deep perineal pouch: below the resolution of a 1 mm frame, same decision and reasoning as the female script (scripts/cryo/vhf_pelvic_floor_from_cryo.py), plus his frame's registration residual is not even independently quantified here (see the module docstring LIMITS) -- if anything a weaker case for attempting it than hers
not_shipped.internal_anal_sphincter: smooth muscle inside the colon label; excluded with it
not_shipped.prostate: not a muscle: TotalSegmentator organ label (id 22), carried only as an exclusion + the urogenital-hiatus landmark (see the module docstring)

levator_ani_right.note: 44.0 cm3; rule-based: the pelvic muscle funnel medial to the obturator internus band, between the pubic arch's apex and 0 mm above the ischial spine; pubococcygeus, puborectalis and iliococcygeus are NOT separated (no septum between them at 1 mm).

coccygeus_right.note: 2.5 cm3; rule-based: the sheet posterior to the anal canal from the ischial spine (level carried from the female by proportion, see levels.ischial_spine.rule) down 6 mm towards the coccyx. His coccyx is NOT labelled either, so the posterior anchor is a 14 mm pad of the bony hull, same limitation as the female script.

bulbospongiosus_right.note: 4.9 cm3; rule-based: over the corpus spongiosum, in the midline behind the scrotum, in the superficial perineal pouch. It is the muscle TOGETHER WITH the corpus spongiosum bulb of the penis it covers: erectile tissue photographs as dark as striated muscle at 1 mm and the two have no septum between them, so the shipped mass is larger than the muscle alone.

ischiocavernosus_right.note: 7.5 cm3; rule-based: on the ischiopubic ramus, in the superficial perineal pouch. It is the muscle TOGETHER WITH the crus of the penis it covers: erectile tissue photographs as dark as striated muscle at 1 mm and the two have no septum between them, so the shipped mass is larger than the muscle alone.

deep_transverse_perineal_right.note: 6.0 cm3; rule-based: position-rule marker relative to his bone and organ labels, boundary by the marker watershed on the pale septa of his cryosection photographs.
